answer: A Sybil swarm stalls at the stake gate. On a terrace of identity slots, every agent must lock a refundable deposit for the whole epoch before it earns, released only after its work clears audit. An honest operator pays once and recovers it. An attacker flooding a thousand wallets must fund a thousand deposits at once along that dune of locked capital, and leaving early burns the stake. Any fraud finding can also slash it. Registering a river of fake identities then costs far more than the rewards they could farm.
